author: Ian Sample and Dan Milmo
description:
Company behind ChatGPT says 10,000 of its AI systems cracked the Navier-Stokes problem in 88 hours

OpenAI claims to have solved a major mathematics problem that has stumped humans for nearly a century after spending millions of dollars on the artificial intelligence-led endeavour.

The company behind ChatGPT said it had cracked the Navier-Stokes problem, one of seven Millennium Prize Problems published by the Clay Mathematics Institute to highlight some of the biggest unsolved puzzles in the field.

Continue reading...
title: OpenAI claims to have solved maths problem that stumped humans for decades

author: Sid Lowe at the Bernabéu
description:
Sometimes football is silly and sometimes it is more fun for it. On a night when there were 37 shots and the goalkeepers shared thirteen saves between them, some of them absurd, José Mourinho’s Real Madrid found a way to beat his former team Inter in his first Champions League night of his second spell. Just don’t ask exactly how. Except perhaps to cite Thibaut Courtois, whose astonishing save in the 89th minute saw them hold on to a 2-0 first-half lead given then by goals from Kylian Mbappé and Fede Valverde themselves. You would say that they had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried, Courtois would probably save that too. This wasn’t always good, in fact at times it was terrible, but they had got through somehow.

You would say that they had shot themselves in the foot, only if they tried, Courtois would probably save that too. This wasn’t always good, in fact at times it was terrible, but they had got through somehow. When Madrid scored the first, this grand aren
title: Mbappé and Valverde fire Real Madrid to Champions League win against Inter

author: Jamie Jackson at Estádio do Dragão
description:
Enzo Maresca admitted a liking for the “boom-boom” of house music, then oversaw a gritty performance that ended with Manchester City enjoying the sweet notes of victory.

They had lost six of their past nine away games in the competition and also lost the 2021 Champions League final at this venue, so to beat Porto and claim three points is a fillip for the manager’s nascent project.

Continue reading...
title: Haaland double gives Manchester City ideal Champions League start in Porto

author: Ben Fisher at the Jan Breydel Stadium
description:
Aston Villa were 3-1 up after 43 minutes but were made to sweat for their first win of the season, emerging victorious from an entertaining Champions League opener against Club Brugge. John McGinn, who struck the only goal when Villa belatedly got their season up and running last September against Bologna, opened the scoring before goals from Emi Buendía and a first for Nicolas Jackson appeared to put Villa out of sight at half-time.

The Belgian side have become familiar foes since Villa returned to the big time, the glitziest club competition of them all; a freakish Tyrone Mings handball gifted the hosts a penalty, and subsequently victory, in 2024-25 and this time Aaron Wan-Bissaka conceded a second-half penalty to plunge a seesawing contest back into the balance. Villa had to live dangerously but equally could have won by a bigger margin.
title: First-half treble powers Aston Villa to Champions League win at Club Brugge

author: Rob Davies
description:
EU’s highest court allows Swedish furniture firm to begin proceedings after Vlaams Belang used its trademarks in immigration campaign

Ikea has won the right to take legal action against a Belgian far-right political party that parodied the Swedish flatpack furniture firm’s branding in its anti-immigration campaign.

In a ruling on Tuesday, Europe’s highest court said that Ikea had the right to oppose the use of its trademarks and distinctive graphics by Vlaams Belang, a rightwing Eurosceptic political party that advocates for an independent Flemish state.

Continue reading...
title: Ikea wins right to launch legal action against Belgian far-right party

author: Ed Aarons
description:
• Team arriving late at their hotel in southern Italy

  • Jurriën Timber in squad for first time since May

Arsenal’s preparations for their opening Champions League game against Napoli have been disrupted after they were caught up in the travel chaos that affected airports across the United Kingdom.

Mikel Arteta was forced to cancel his pre-match press conference at the Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on Tuesday after Arsenal’s flight was severely delayed by an air-traffic control issue. The Arsenal manager and his players are understood to have remained at the club’s training ground in Hertfordshire as they waited for the delay to pass after completing their morning session as usual.

Continue read
title: Air traffic chaos delays Arsenal flight to Naples for Champions League

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Foreign secretary ends UK’s feigned helplessness with sanctions and condemnation of ‘ethnic cleansing’

  • Will UK sanctions have any impact on ‘settler terrorists’?

The indefatigable ability of UK Foreign Office ministers over decades to issue boilerplate statements of concern about the extension of illegal settlements in Israel has long been a matter of ridicule.

Even some of the Conservative ministers who issued them, notably Alan Duncan and Alistair Burt, have agreed. Duncan described the UK stance towards settlements as weak and naive, while Burt wondered at the ability of the Foreign Office to find new forms of diplomatic condemnation that never amounted to any specific action. Margaret Thatcher, often torn as prime minister between her natural sympathy for Israel and her fear of the Gulf states falling under the sway of the Soviet Un
title: Ed Miliband has overturned decades of Foreign Office inertia on illegal Israeli settlements

author: Adrian Horton
description:
Satirical program’s new title is ‘inspired by bravery and patriotism’ of Apple and Google, who capitulated to Trump’s requests to change Lake Ontario to ‘Lake America’

In light of Donald Trump’s attempts to rename a gulf, lakes and even states after “America”, South Park, the animated satirical program that has long skewered those in power, has announced an official name change. For its 29th season, the Comedy Central series will be known as “South America”.

“Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of South Park to SOUTH AMERICA,” creators Matt Stone and Trey Parker said in a statement. “We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount – a Skydance Capitulation.” The show’s parent company, Par
title: South Park changes name to South America in response to Trump changes

author: Daniel Harris
description:
• Champions League: Lille v Betis, Dortmund v Villarreal

  • Carabao Cup: Palace v Middlesbroigh, Sunderland v Hull

  • Live scores | Read Football Daily | And email Daniel

Goodness me, there’s a lot going on. In Bruges, Villa are going nicely…

On 16 September 1987, Diego Maradona’s Napoli travelled to La Quinta del Buitre’s Real Madrid to play a first round, first leg match of the European Cup. Madrid won 2-0 with the return at the San Paolo drawn 1-1, meaning elimination for I Partenopei, gone from the competition almost before they arrived.

Contin
title: Real Madrid v Inter, Millwall v Newcastle: Champions League and Carabao Cup – live

author: Chris Stein in Washington
description:
‘I have to be honest, it has been stressful,’ Lonnie Bunch III says

The Smithsonian Institution’s secretary, Lonnie Bunch III, will retire at the end of the year amid Donald Trump’s attacks on the museum’s content and independence.

Bunch, who was appointed in 2019 as the first African American to lead the museums, cited personal reasons for departing, while acknowledging the pressure that the president’s attacks on the Smithsonian’s depictions of US history had taken.

Continue reading...
title: Smithsonian Institution secretary to retire amid Trump attacks on museum independence

author: John Crace
description:
Opposition to Miliband’s announcement of sanctions rings hollow – helped by fewer than 10 Tory backbenchers turning up to debate

Nobody can say they weren’t warned. The Andy Burnham government might have looked like Continuity Keir with more positive vibes for the first six weeks or so, but on Tuesday a new line was drawn. When Burnham said he felt Labour had not done enough on Palestine and Gaza, he had meant it. His decision to impose trade sanctions on illegal settlements in the West Bank was to be his first break with the past.

Some opponents chose to get their retaliation in early, before Ed Miliband had even stood up to make the announcement in the Commons on Tuesday. Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador, declared on Sunday that Ed was guilty of “hating Jews”. Which rather implied he thought Ed hated himself.
title: Commons breathes a sigh of relief as UK finally takes a moral stance of Israeli settlements | John Crace

author: Victoria Bekiempis
description:
Appeals court dismisses lawsuit from Jackson residents claiming that tainted drinking water violated their rights

A US appellate court has decided that the federal constitution does not guarantee a right to clean water.

That legal opinion came in the form of a decision on Friday from the fifth circuit court of appeals to uphold a lower court’s dismissal of a 2022 lawsuit from several Jackson, Mississippi, residents claiming that tainted drinking water violated their constitutional rights.

Continue reading...
title: US federal court says no constitutional right to clean water in Mississippi case

author: Ella Baron
description: Continue reading...
title: Ella Baron on the UK’s ban on trade with illegal Israeli settlements – cartoon

author: Editorial
description:
Ed Miliband has delivered Britain’s toughest indictment of Israeli conduct in Palestinian lands - and rightly says this has economic consequences

Rarely in recent years has the Commons felt like the cockpit of history. On Tuesday it did. The foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, placed Britain at the head of a 12-country coalition considering economic restrictions on Israel’s illegal settlements, with the UK, France and Canada committing to national trade bans.

The move comes after escalating numbers of attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinian villages in the West Bank. International opinion seemed to shift decisively after Israel gave the go-ahead for 1,200 homes in the E1 settlement that would cleave the West Bank into two – using illegal settlements to bury Palestinian statehood for good. Mr Milib
title: The Guardian view on Britain’s new Middle East policy: an unlawful occupation must carry a price | Editorial

author: Ben Beaumont-Thomas
description:
Tickets set to cost £408 at return for Somerset festival after a fallow year, a jump from £378.50 in 2025

After a fallow year in 2026, Glastonbury festival fans can start to get excited – and nervous – about tickets for 2027’s event going on sale.

The price breaks £400 for the first time, at £408 including a £5 booking fee, a rise from the 2025 cost of £378.50. The usual scramble to acquire them – with all the attendant frantic spreadsheets and WhatsApp groups – will begin at 9am on Sunday 4 October.

Continue reading...
title: Glastonbury tickets break £400 for first time as on-sale date is announced

author: Niall McVeigh
description:
⚽ Champions League updates from the 8pm BST kick-off
⚽ Live scores | Read Football Daily | And you can mail Niall

Manchester City’s Enzo Maresca era has got off to a decent start, with three wins from three in the Premier League. The Champions League will offer a sterner test than their domestic opposition so far, with PSG, Barcelona, Napoli and plenty more top-tier teams dropping into their autumn fixture list.

First up, though, is a September trip to Porto – nice for the fans, not so much for the City players. Also managed by a tactically cautious Italian in Francesco Farioli, the Portuguese champions also boast a 100% league record this season. With the Manchester derby up next, the hard work starts here for
title: Porto v Manchester City: Champions League – live

author: Ewan Murray in Bernadus, Netherlands
description:
• Teetotal Hull teed off alone in practice

  • Briton in Women’s Open controversy in August

Charley Hull has, unsurprisingly, been involved in a colourful start to Solheim Cup week. After arriving late for her Tuesday practice tee time in the Netherlands, an online clip of her joking about the reason prompted a cascade of online speculation and ended with members of the European team hierarchy forcibly denying any overindulgence on the teetotal Hull’s behalf on Monday night.

In an unusual scene, Hull, who is crucial to Europe’s quest to reclaim the Solheim Cup from the United States this week, drove off alone at Bernardus Golf and caught up with her teammates after arriving on the 1st tee minutes behind them. In a clip that gained traction, Hull appeared to jokingly blame “drinks” from the night before. The English golfer did, however, seem to point towards her caddie at the time.
title: Solheim Cup vice-captain denies Charley Hull’s late arrival due to ‘drinks’

author: Richard Luscombe in Miami
description:
The victims, employees of an aircraft cleaning company, were in a van when the plane crashed into it

  • At least five dead after Amazon cargo plane crashes at Miami airport

Officials in Florida on Tuesday identified the five people killed in Saturday’s Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami international airport – and said two more remained hospitalized in critical condition.

At a morning news conference, the Miami-Dade sheriff, Rosie Cordero-Stutz, also said both pilots of the Amazon Prime Air Boeing 767, which careered off the end of the airport’s runway and struck at least two vehicles, were released from the hospital after treatment.
title: Victims of deadly Amazon cargo plane crash identified, as two more remain critical

author: Associated Press
description:
Islands of Kauai and Ni’ihau are under hurricane warning, while Oahu is under a tropical storm warning

Damaging winds and heavy rains from Hurricane Lowell were pelting Hawaii’s western islands on Tuesday, bringing the threat of floods, mudslides and tornadoes.

The islands of Kauai and Ni’ihau are under a hurricane warning, while Oahu, the state’s most populated island with close to 1 million residents, was under a tropical storm warning.

Continue reading...
title: Hurricane Lowell brings threat of floods, mudslides and tornadoes to Hawaii

author: Oliver Milman
description:
Attorney hopes Trump would ‘consider a pardon’ given ‘the type of person she is’ and ‘what she has been through’

Murder trial ends in dramatic deadlock – what comes next

The lawyer of Lindsay Clancy, the Massachusetts woman accused of killing her three young children, has said he hopes Donald Trump will pardon his client after her trial recently ended with a deadlocked jury.

Clancy’s attorney, Kevin Reddington, made the appeal on a televised interview on the ABC show Good Morning America on Tuesday. The plea comes to Trump after a judge on Friday declared a mistrial after the jury in the Clancy case could not reach a unanimous verdict on whether she was guilty or not guilty.

<
title: Lindsay Clancy’s lawyer urges Trump to consider pardon after mistrial

author: Margaret Sullivan
description:
The more defense secretary Pete Hegseth tries to flex his manly strength, the wimpier he looks

The more the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, tries to flex his manly strength, the wimpier he looks.

The former Fox News host has attempted to seize control of what the public is allowed to know, but bad news keeps creeping out from the Pentagon.

Margaret Sullivan is a Guardian US columnist

Continue reading...
title: Mass polygraphs at the Pentagon show Hegseth’s weakness | Margaret Sullivan

author: Peter Beaumont Senior international correspondent
description:
Israeli PM says allegation that UAE president alerted him more than a week before major offensive is ‘absolute lie’

Benjamin Netanyahu was personally alerted by the president of the United Arab Emirates that Hamas was planning a large-scale offensive against Israel a week before its 7 October 2023 attack, but did not act on the warning, according to a book by Haaretz reporters.

The claim, which comes amid a crucial election campaign, prompted Israeli opposition leaders to describe the prime minister as “unfit” for office, even as Netanyahu denounced the report as an “absolute lie” and denied he spoke to the Emirati leader at that time.

Continue reading...
title: Netanyahu was warned of 7 October Hamas attacks, book claims

author: Geneva Abdul
description:
Mira Lozi says quiet diplomacy has failed to free Rami Naimi who was first seized in Dubai in 2017

A British woman has spoken out for the first time about the alleged abduction, torture and coercion of her husband at the hands of Saudi authorities, after nine years of “failed” quiet diplomacy.

The businessman Rami Naimi was first abducted in Dubai in 2017 on his return from a trip to Australia with his father. After being tortured, he was released the following year.

Continue reading...
title: British family speaks out over nine-year ordeal after husband is abducted by Saudi Arabia

author: Katy Murrells (now) and Taha Hashim (later)
description:
Rolling updates from the last eight at Flushing Meadows
Will influencers bring down US Open? | You can mail Katy

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the US Open - day 10!

So here we are, at the quarter-final stage. Gone is the compelling chaos of matches taking place here, there and everywhere in the earlier rounds, and finally we can make do with only one pair of eyes, our gaze both shrinking and intensifying now we’re down to the one singles court.

Continue reading...
title: US Open 2026 quarter-finals: Sabalenka v Noskova, Tiafoe v Michelsen – live

author: Oliver Milman
description:
David Burke’s defense argues there is no evidence he had any intent of killing 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez

The family of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez has called for the singer D4vd, who is on trial suspected of killing the girl, to face the death penalty.

D4vd, who was born David Anthony Burke, in July was ordered to stand trial over the killing of Rivas, whose dismembered body was found in the trunk of his Tesla car on 8 September 2025. Burke has pleaded not guilty to the charges.

Continue reading...
title: Family of slain teen calls for death penalty in murder trial of singer D4vd

author: Peter Beaumont
description:
Riyadh says it will retaliate after overnight attacks by Iran-backed Yemen group on oil facilities wound more than 70

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have attacked four cities in Saudi Arabia, wounding more than 70 people and setting oil installations ablaze in what appeared to be a significant expansion of the Middle East war.

Saudi Arabia said it would retaliate after the overnight strikes – reportedly involving dozens of drones and missiles – that targeted several oil facilities in the country’s south.

Continue reading...
title: Houthis strike Saudi Arabian cities in significant expansion of Middle East war

author: Ezra Levin and Leah Greenberg
description:
Candidates must focus on two issues: affordability and accountability. They are not competing priorities

As the November election approaches with control of the House and Senate on the line, the stakes are high. With so much riding on the outcome, there is no shortage of debate about the message Democrats need to win.

Affordability has emerged as a shared – if often undefined – rallying cry. Working families are struggling with rising costs and looking for answers. But too often, we’ve seen affordability positioned as the beginning and end of the plan. Meanwhile, many see holding the Trump administration accountable for its corruption and harms as at odds with a relentless focus on kitchen-table issues.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats need to win. Here’s the message our research says works

author: Oliver Milman
description:
From rare bacteria to ‘forever chemicals’, a series of cases of violations or alleged pollution has prompted alarm

When officials in Wyoming conducted a routine test on the water that was being discharged from a massive under-construction Meta datacenter, it was a shock to find it contained a rare and potentially hazardous bacterium.

While the wastewater flushed into sewers in Cheyenne, Wyoming, was never destined for the public drinking supply, the presence of Cupriavidus gilardii bacterium in 801,000 gallons of water ejected by a contractor for the datacenter earlier this year was still unnerving.

Continue reading...
title: US datacenters face further backlash over wastewater pollution

author: Stephanie Kaloi
description:
Players generally welcome interacting with their fans. But as the league’s popularity surges, there are dangers to be aware of

Caitlin Clark spent most of the 2025 WNBA season sidelined with a series of injuries that forced her to miss more than 30 games. But she also spent part of the season (and the preceding offseason) quietly navigating a tumultuous and scary reality: a 55-year-old man was stalking her, and he was convinced they were in a relationship.

That man, Michael Lewis, was sentenced to two-and-a-half years in prison last July. Lewis sent Clark “hundreds” of messages – many of which were “threats and sexually explicit” – between 12 December 2024 and 11 January 2025. Lewis, who is from Texas, was arrested at a hotel in Indianapol
title: Caitlin Clark and Sophie Cunningham have been stalked. They’re far from alone in the WNBA

author: Jakub Krupa
description:
Ruslan Kravchenko leaves post after his offices were searched at the weekend, as Moscow renews attacks after pause for peace talks

Iceland summoned the US ambassador for talks last night after US president Donald Trump posted on social media an AI-generated map of the US, Canada and other countries, which appeared to include Iceland as the US territory.

Icelandic national broadcaster RÚV reported that the ambassador was told that the post was “completely inappropriate.”

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine’s prosecutor general resigns after corruption allegations as Russia resumes strikes on Kyiv – Europe live

author: Douglas Smith
description:
Mount Isa city council to auction off first of 24 homes after Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Corporation for Welfare Services accrues almost $1m in unpaid debts

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A rural Queensland council is auctioning off 24 homes to recover unpaid rates, potentially forcing First Nations families into homelessness.

Residents claim they were left in the dark about the debt, which stretches back years, until five months
title: ‘Forced out with nowhere to go’: First Nations families face eviction as council sells homes over charity’s unpaid rates

author: James Borrowdale in Auckland
description:
Despite just missing out on the minor premiership, fans are daring to dream as the Wahs emerge as the most-loved rugby team in the city

From the concourse above Go Media Stadium’s northern bank, in the hour before kick-off, the New Zealand Warriors final game of the regular season seems almost incidental. The late-afternoon, early-spring sunshine paints the deep shadow of the Colin Kay Stand over the turf far below, where the NRLW fixture splutters to its conclusion, and the talk of fans leapfrogsbeyond the upcoming men’s game against Manly.

Paul Miller, a Warriors fan since the team’s inaugural 1995 season, leans against a metal railing, a grin playing on his lips. He won’t quite claim it to be “our year” just yet, but his wallet has already spoken for him. He will be in the stands of Sydney’s Accor Stadium come 4 October – and he anticipates that his team will be with him. “We’ve already got grand final tickets, so we’re pretty hopeful.”
title: ‘We’ve got grand final tickets’: Belief builds in Auckland amid Warriors NRL fever | James Borrowdale

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
Researchers urge governments to help worst afflicted countries, such as Nigeria and Algeria, which rely on oil revenues for public services

Conflict, migration and economic upheaval will accompany the global move away from oil, unless governments act urgently to help the worst afflicted countries to cope, research has found.

Nigeria, Iran, Angola and Algeria are among the countries that will be severely affected, as they rely strongly on oil revenues for their government and provision of public services, but have little diversification and too little capital to cushion the blow.

Continue reading...
title: Global move away from oil could lead to conflict and migration, experts say
